paragraphs.text: Strategic Role: India's undisputed corporate capital for the processing, polishing, and packaging of Barnyard Millet (Vari/Bhagar). Handles over 70% of the country's commercial festival fasting grain trade.

Key Facilities: Automated milling plants across Igatpuri, Trimbakeshwar, Ghoti, and Nashik MIDC; high-capacity trichromatic optical color sorters, pneumatic destoners, and modified atmosphere packaging lines supplying major brands (e.g., Bhagar King, Ghoti Brand).

Catchment Areas: Nashik, Palghar, Thane, and Pune crestlines (Maharashtra); interstate rail receipts of raw un-hulled Jhangora from the Himalayan foothills of Uttarakhand (Rishikesh, Kotdwar railheads); border inflows from Dangs (Gujarat).

paragraphs.text: 3. Central Tribal Decentralized Processing Basin (Madhya Pradesh & Odisha)
Strategic Role: India's primary production heartland for Kodo and Little Millet, focused on rural value retention and food security under GI tags and state missions.
Key Centers: Dindori, Mandla, and Bichhiya (MP); Semiliguda, Kundra, and Gunupur (Odisha).

Infrastructure Profile: Community-managed Custom Hiring and Processing Centers (CHPCs) operated by Women Self-Help Groups (WSHGs); rubber-roller dehullers and destoners established under the Odisha Millets Mission and MP state tribal development federations.
Catchment Areas: Dindori, Mandla, Shahdol, Anuppur, Chhindwara (MP); Koraput, Rayagada, Malkangiri, Nabarangpur (Odisha); Bastar and Kondagaon plateaus (Chhattisgarh).

protection.name: Kodo Head Blight / "Kodo Poisoning" (Aspergillus flavus, Claviceps paspali, Fusarium spp.)
protection.geography: All Kodo-Growing Belts (Heavy in MP, Chhattisgarh)
protection.impact: Grains infected with toxigenic fungi during damp, overcast harvest weather accumulate toxic mycotoxins (cyclopiazonic acid - CPA); consumption of molded grain causes intoxication, tremors, nausea, and central nervous depression in humans and cattle ("Kodrah poisoning").
protection.passage: Small Millets — source table 118, row 2. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Millet Blast (Pyricularia setariae / Magnaporthe grisea)
protection.geography: All-India Minor Millet Tracts (Severe in Foxtail & Little Millet)
protection.impact: Spindle-shaped lesions with ash-grey centers and brown borders appear on leaves; lesions coalesce, causing foliar drying; necrotic black lesions girdle the neck of the panicle (Neck Blast), causing earheads to break off and grains to remain empty and chaffy.
protection.passage: Small Millets — source table 118, row 3. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Grain Smut / Head Smut (Ustilago crameri, Sorosporium spp.)
protection.impact: Individual ovaries or entire panicle spikelets are transformed into enlarged, dark brown-to-black sacks of fungal chlamydospores; sori rupture during threshing, coating healthy grains in foul black dust; destroys 10–40% of grain yield.
protection.passage: Small Millets — source table 118, row 4. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Atherigona Shoot Fly Complex (Atherigona soccata, A. pulla)
protection.geography: Early Vegetative Stage (All Minor Millet Belts)
protection.impact: Tiny whitish maggots bore into the central growing point of 7-to-20-day-old seedlings; central leaf turns yellow, wilts, and dries up, forming a foul-smelling "Dead Heart" that pulls out easily; causes stunted, bushy, unproductive tillers.
protection.passage: Small Millets — source table 118, row 5. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Spotted Stem Borer (Chilo partellus) & Rust (Uromyces setariae-italicae)
protection.impact: Borer larvae chew pinholes in leaf whorls and tunnel down the culm, causing stem breakage; rust causes minute, reddish-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces, leading to early foliar drying.
protection.passage: Small Millets — source table 118, row 6. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.

protection.name: Rice Weevil & Rust-Red Flour Beetle (Sitophilus oryzae, Tribolium castaneum)
protection.impact: Weevils and larvae bore into stored dehulled minor millet rice; hollow out grains, generating flour dust, webbing, and foul odors; un-hulled raw paddy exhibits significantly higher natural resistance to storage pests.
protection.passage: Small Millets — source table 118, row 7. Management modes are descriptive; formulations, rates and schedules omitted.
